title: Incremental ingestion and change detection
summary: Incremental ingestion processes only what changed since the last run, using a timestamp, a change log or a content hash, and falls back to a full rebuild when the pipeline itself changes.
useIf: The corpus is large, changes slowly relative to its size and you want cost and run time to follow the changes, not the corpus.
avoidIf: The corpus is small or the source gives no reliable change signal: a scheduled full reload is simpler and safer.

explain.md: A change signal answers one question: what is different since my last run? **Timestamps** are the cheapest. The Blob indexer uses `LastModified` [[tr4]], and the Cosmos DB indexer uses a high-water mark on `_ts` [[tr6]]. Azure SQL offers **integrated change tracking** (tables only, detects deleted rows, recommended) or a **high-water mark** on a `rowversion` or last-updated column, which also works for views [[tr5]]. A **content hash** compares what you stored with what you have read now, so an item that was touched but not edited costs no embedding call.

Signals have blind spots. Deletes are not tracked by default for Blob, and both Blob and Cosmos DB need a soft-delete policy from the first run [[tr4]] [[tr6]]. A restored blob is not re-indexed unless its `LastModified` changes, and renaming an ADLS Gen2 directory does not update blob timestamps [[tr4]]. The fix for any source with blind spots is a periodic **reconciliation**: list source ids, list index keys, and repair the difference.

Incremental runs are not enough when the pipeline changes. A new parser, chunker or embedding model changes every chunk, so you need a full rebuild into a new index (see the blue-green topic). For targeted replays, Reset Indexer is the GA full reset, while Reset Documents, Reset Skills and Resync are preview APIs in `2026-08-01-preview` [[tr9]].

steps.md: Ask the source for items newer than the checkpoint, or read the change log.

steps.title: Hash gate
steps.md: Skip items whose normalised content hash is unchanged.

steps.title: Process
steps.md: Parse, chunk and embed only the changed items.

steps.title: Upsert
steps.md: Write with a stable key so a replay is safe.

steps.title: Reconcile and advance
steps.md: Repair missing or extra ids, then move the checkpoint.

whereToUse: Large document stores where a small percentage changes each day
Database-backed catalogues with a rowversion, last-updated column or change tracking
Content that is touched by tools (migrations, virus scans) without real edits, where a hash gate saves embedding cost
Nightly reconciliation jobs that compare source ids with index keys
Pipelines that run both incremental updates and rare planned full rebuilds

use: Use built-in indexer change detection when the source is a supported GA store
Use SQL integrated change tracking on tables when deletes matter
Use a content hash when timestamps are noisy or edits are cosmetic
Use periodic reconciliation whenever the source can hard-delete or move items
avoid: Avoid timestamp-only detection when files are restored, renamed in bulk or touched by other tools
Avoid incremental runs after a parser, chunker or model change: rebuild instead
Avoid enabling soft-delete handling after the first run and expecting history to be corrected
flips: Corpus is small and cheap to re-embed: a nightly full reload removes whole classes of bugs
Source offers a true change log (SQL change tracking or an all-versions change feed): prefer it to timestamps
Pipeline code changed: schedule a full rebuild into a new index

pitfalls.symptom: A restored file never reappears in search
pitfalls.cause: Restoring a soft-deleted blob does not change `LastModified`, so the indexer sees nothing new
pitfalls.fix: Touch the blob or reset the document, and document the restore procedure

pitfalls.symptom: Reorganised ADLS folders are missing from answers
pitfalls.cause: Renaming a directory does not update the timestamps of the blobs inside it
pitfalls.fix: Reset the indexer or reprocess the moved folder after bulk moves

pitfalls.symptom: Deleted source items stay in the index
pitfalls.cause: No soft-delete policy existed on the first indexer run, or the source hard-deletes
pitfalls.fix: Add the policy and flag-then-delete, or reconcile ids on a schedule

pitfalls.symptom: Embedding bills spike after a storage migration
pitfalls.cause: A migration tool rewrote timestamps so every file looks changed
pitfalls.fix: Gate on a content hash before parse and embed

scenarios.title: Two million files, 0.1 percent daily churn
scenarios.situation: A knowledge base holds two million files and about 0.1 percent change each day. Embedding spend must follow the change rate, not the corpus size.
unknowns: Do files get restored or renamed in bulk?
scenarios.question: How do you keep the index current?

options.name: Indexer change detection with a soft-delete policy, plus a weekly id reconciliation
options.why: Timestamps keep daily cost proportional to changes and reconciliation catches moves and hard deletes.
options.tradeoff: You maintain the soft-delete convention and the reconciliation job.

options.name: Nightly full rebuild
options.why: It re-embeds 2 million files to pick up about 2,000 changes.
options.tradeoff: Right for a small corpus or after a pipeline change.

options.name: Timestamps only, no deletes handling
options.why: Cheapest to run and covers edits.
options.tradeoff: Deleted, restored and moved files drift out of sync.

flips.if: Corpus shrinks to a few thousand files

flips.then: Add a content hash gate before embedding.

scenarios.takeaway: Let cost follow churn, then add a safety net for what timestamps cannot see.

scenarios.title: Noisy timestamps after a migration
scenarios.situation: A storage migration touched half a million files without editing them. The next incremental run would re-embed all of them. Budget is limited and the content is unchanged.
unknowns: Is a hash of each file already stored?
How expensive is reading a file compared with embedding it?
scenarios.question: What do you do before the run?

options.name: Compare content hashes and skip files whose hash matches the stored one
options.why: Reading and hashing is far cheaper than parsing and embedding, and unchanged files are skipped.
options.tradeoff: You need stored hashes and stable normalisation.

options.name: Let the indexer re-process everything
options.why: No new code and a clean result.
options.tradeoff: Pays full embedding cost for no new information.

options.name: Disable change detection and rebuild monthly
options.why: It trades one cost for a month of staleness and loses delete handling.

flips.then: Compute them once during this run, then use them from now on.

scenarios.takeaway: A hash gate turns noisy signals into correct decisions.

quiz.q: Which Azure SQL change detection option is recommended for tables and also detects deleted rows?
quiz.explain: Integrated change tracking works on tables and sees deletes. A high-water mark works for views but needs a soft-delete column. Full reload and `LastModified` are not SQL indexer policies.

quiz.q: A corpus has 2,000,000 files, 0.1 percent change per day and about 12 chunks per file. How many chunks are embedded per day with perfect incremental ingestion?
quiz.explain: 0.1 percent of 2,000,000 is 2,000 files. Multiplied by 12 chunks gives 24,000 chunks per day, compared with 24,000,000 for a full rebuild.

quiz.q: Which situations leave the Blob indexer unaware of a change?
options: An ADLS Gen2 directory is renamed
A blob body is edited and `LastModified` updates
A blob is hard-deleted with no soft-delete policy
quiz.explain: Restores and directory renames do not change `LastModified`, and hard deletes are invisible without a policy. A normal edit updates `LastModified` and is detected.

flashcards.front: Why is a content hash a useful gate in incremental ingestion?
flashcards.back: It skips items that were touched but not changed, so parse and embedding cost follow real edits, not timestamps.

flashcards.front: SQL indexer: integrated change tracking versus high-water mark?
flashcards.back: Change tracking: tables only, sees deletes, recommended. High-water mark: rowversion or last-updated column, works for views, needs a soft-delete column for deletes.

flashcards.front: Which indexer reset is GA, and which are preview?
flashcards.back: Reset Indexer is GA. Reset Documents, Reset Skills and Resync are preview APIs in `2026-08-01-preview`.
